std::atomic_file.note: Bounded sequential publication implemented in Lanius over TempFile and existing Linux descriptor calls. Keep one in-place manual owner; destination bytes are copied before effects. Replace/NoReplace commit syncs and closes the file once, renames once, immediately records Published/disarms deletion, then syncs the anchored directory. Receipts preserve NotPublished/Published/Unconfirmed visibility, confirmed bytes, current resources and separate primary/latest/cleanup errors. Cached commit is inert; explicit directory-sync retry never writes or renames. Failed removal retains recovery ownership; cleanup never unlinks the destination. Native Linux x86_64/kernel 7.0.0-38-generic/ext4 under /tmp passes owner 9, bounds 25, publication 6 and faults 26: 66 process invocations across four groups including baselines; preliminary smoke overlaps. A live-anchor Published checkpoint precedes ACK-controlled explicit sync retry. The bounds retry fixes only the oracle owned-fd write selector and reuses the unchanged probe ELF. Thirty-six CPU ledger controls and Rust --no-run admission are separate from native execution. Actual source/fd ownership is observed before exit. Parent mutation authority must be exclusive/cooperative; attempts/bytes are bounded, blocking time is not. No hostile-directory, network-filesystem, locking, universal power-loss or automatic-destructor guarantee; no new runtime binding or crypto implementation.

std::command.note: Process-group creation is explicit. Group signaling requires the confirmed original group and an owned, unreaped leader; non-reaping terminal observations do not consume that anchor. Final reaping or lost-child evidence revokes it. Copied Child descriptors do not grant independent wait or signal authority. The guides define startup uncertainty, cancellation limits and current target/execution evidence.

std::command_capture.note: Progress.status may be an observed terminal status while Progress.reaped is false. Capture retains the unreaped leader anchor while draining acquired pipes, then performs a charged final nonblocking reap before success. A failure can retain that Child authority unless ownership was lost or final reaping already occurred; captured output owners and child cleanup remain explicit. The guides define operation/deadline scope and current execution evidence.

std::file_ops.note: Checked Linux x86_64 descriptor operations over std::linux, with owned File handles and explicit one-attempt host errors. remove_file_at and rename_at use unlinkat/renameat2, Replace/NoReplace, complete path staging and no retry/existence-check/copy fallback. Their earlier primitive group passes 27 process invocations on kernel 7.0.0-38-generic/ext4 under /tmp; preliminary bounds evidence overlaps. The earlier allocation-free create_dir_at/remove_dir_at use mkdirat/unlinkat(AT_REMOVEDIR), validate full path/mode before one attempt and preserve caller ownership. Their three focused native groups pass namespace24/bounds19/faults12 process invocations, including two repeated baselines and reached errno/invalid-count injections. General host path resolution still applies; EEXIST is not proof of a safe directory. These primitives supply no durability, automatic rollback or hostile-directory authority. TempFile and AtomicFile apply their separate cooperative namespace/publication/recovery contracts. Nine additional link/readlink and descriptor/path permission functions plus LinkRead are accepted at source freeze 21269e34 on the documented native Linux x86_64/ext4 profile. Both paths are staged before link/symlink effects; bounded readlink uses a private packed probe and validates its returned count before caller-buffer mutation, with explicit incomplete status when the probe fills. Mode validation precedes descriptor/path admission; raw fchmodat has three arguments and follows the final symlink. These one-attempt allocation-free additions are not covered by the earlier primitive receipts. Their five groups pass links 28, readlink 19, permissions 12, bounds 45 and faults 35, totaling 139 accepted group cases across separate commands. The first 34 fault cases repeat in the successful fault-only retry, which replaced an unlaunchable large strace poke with a known 16-byte prefix/full-count control; real readlink outputs remain fully compared. Native syscall instruction provenance and zero source allocation are checked. The initial comparison/cast parser ambiguity was isolated and expressed with an equivalent widening-cast local, without compiler changes. Injected skipped closes establish logical retirement rather than physical close success.

std::temp_dir.note: Named temporary-directory ownership implemented in Lanius at source freeze 56898b00, with all four groups accepted: owner 9, admission/entropy 19, creation faults 8 and cleanup faults 10. These total 46 accepted group cases across three native commands, not cumulative executions; oracle retries repeat earlier cases. Callback shadowing and a duplicate getrandom injection rule were harness defects, corrected without production changes. The final entropy control binds one first-draw injection and verifies real subsequent entropy. One manual owner reserves its name, retains a CLOEXEC parent duplicate, uses bounded OS entropy for exclusive mkdir, records removal duty before the child open, and never recursively deletes children. Nonempty/removal failure preserves remaining child/parent/name resources for explicit retry or same-owner keep. Close attempts retire descriptors once, preserving separate primary and cleanup errors. Parent namespaces must be cooperative; no hostile-name, crash scavenging, automatic-destruction or broader-platform guarantee follows. Earlier TempFile and archive-directory receipts do not establish this distinct mkdir/open/removal lifecycle. The real mktemp_dir application separately passes all four tests: normal 5, arguments 13, allocations 4 and faults 26, totaling 48 process invocations across two native Linux x86_64/kernel7.0.0-38/ext4-/tmp receipts, with overlapping setup/baselines. Allocation cases include all three reached source OOMs; actual closed-reader help/creation pipes require native EPIPE. The application source is 118f9a78 with FileOps 21269e34. Sixteen CPU controls and driver build admission remain separate. Skipped-close injections establish logical retirement and expose physically open descriptors until exit. TempDir controls number 45, separately from native execution. Owner 9 is accepted within a mixed 6.88-second command, creation 8/cleanup 10 within a mixed 7.66-second command and admission 19 in 6.07 seconds; mixed-command times include other harness failures, not isolated passing-group durations.

std::temp_file.note: Named temporary-file ownership implemented in Lanius over bounded OS entropy and existing Linux calls. Keep one manual TempFile owner; creation retains a CLOEXEC directory duplicate, validates directory metadata/flags and exclusively creates a 0600 no-follow file from a fresh 16-byte OS-entropy candidate. Destination exclusion occurs before open. Same-owner keep disarms deletion without I/O; file close retires once; failed removal retains name/anchor authority for explicit retry or keep. Parent namespaces must be exclusive/cooperative, not hostile. Combined TempFile/FileOps acceptance covers 78 process invocations across owner 8/collisions 6/validation 18/faults 19/primitives 27 on native Linux x86_64/kernel 7.0.0-38-generic/ext4 under /tmp, including repeated baselines rather than distinct behaviors. Faults reach one 37-byte dynamic source OOM; 26 CPU controls and three verified runtime pairs per ELF support source/fd ledgers and applicable pre-exit ownership checks. Cargo --no-run driver admission is separate from native execution. AtomicFile, kv_tool migration, crash durability and scavenging remain outside this checkpoint. No cryptographic algorithm or new runtime binding is added.
